A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the left ventricular geometry and the left ventricular mass are important predictors of the severity of the left ventricular hypertrophic changes in children and adolescents suffering from essential hypertension.

the results of this study support the notion that left ventricular hypertrophic patterns in children with essential hypertension are similar to those observed in adults, and that the left ventricular geometry of children with severe hypertrophy is similar to those of adults with severe hypertrophy.
the results of our study suggest that the left ventricular geometry in children with essential hypertension is more frequently abnormal than previously reported.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the left ventricular mass in hypertensive children is significantly higher than that of healthy children.

the use of a single, simple, inexpensive, and noninvasive measure of left ventricular mass can be used to detect and predict the presence of severe hypertension and the presence of left ventricular hypertrophic response in children and adolescents.

the use of a combination of a diuretic and an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor in patients with severe hypertension and LVH may be more effective in reducing left ventricular mass than either agent alone, even though the combination is less effective at reducing blood pressure.
